Slide.Title: under (preposition)
Slide.SlideText: under (preposition) Definition: Definition: below; below the surface of Synonyms: Synonyms: beneath, underneath Examples: Examples: The river flows under the bridge. It’s cold. She’s wearing two sweaters under her coat. He’s hiding under the table. He’s hiding under the table.

Slide.Title: understand (verb)
Slide.SlideText: understand (verb) Definition: Definition: to know what is meant; to have knowledge of Synonyms: Synonyms: comprehend, grasp, follow Examples: Examples: I don’t understand what you mean. We couldn’t understand what the baby was trying to say. She doesn’t understand how to use a computer. She doesn’t understand how to use a computer.

Slide.Title: unite (verb)
Slide.SlideText: unite (verb) Definition: Definition: to join together Synonyms: Synonyms: combine, blend Examples: Examples: All the neighbors united to clean up the park. In 2008, Delta and Northwest airlines united to form the world’s largest airline. The workers united to solve the problem. The workers united to solve the problem.

Slide.Title: universe (noun)
Slide.SlideText: universe (noun) Definition: Definition: all of space, including the planets and stars Synonyms: Synonyms: cosmos Examples: Examples: There are billions of stars in the universe. How old is the universe? The universe is endless. The universe is endless.

Slide.Title: university (noun)
Slide.SlideText: university (noun) Definition: Definition: a place of education that usually includes several colleges and research organizations Synonyms: Synonyms: college, school Examples: Examples: Her dream is to go to a university in England. Dr. Pham is a professor at the university. My daughter graduated from the university today. My daughter graduated from the university today.

Slide.Title: unless (conjunction)
Slide.SlideText: unless (conjunction) Definition: Definition: except if (something) happens; except that Synonyms: Synonyms: but, if not Examples: Examples: You can’t park in a handicapped parking space unless you have a special permit. Unless I hear from you, I’ll plan to meet you at 5. I will not go unless it stops raining. I will not go unless it stops raining.

Slide.Title: until (conjunction)
Slide.SlideText: until (conjunction) Definition: Definition: up to a certain time Synonyms: Synonyms: to Examples: Examples: Last night we worked until 10 p.m. The children played outside until dark. The card was valid until January, 2006. The card was valid until January, 2006.

Slide.Title: up (adverb)
Slide.SlideText: up (adverb) Definition: Definition: in, at, or to a higher level or position; opposite of “down” Synonyms: Synonyms: above, higher Examples: Examples: The cost of gasoline keeps on going up. The cat climbed up the tree. When I was small, my father used to throw me up in the air. When I was small, my father used to throw me up in the air.

Slide.Title: urge (verb)
Slide.SlideText: urge (verb) Definition: Definition: to advise strongly Synonyms: Synonyms: beg, entreat, plead Examples: Examples: Sheila urged her son to take an umbrella. The doctor urged the patient to stop smoking. She urged her parents to let her go out with her friends. She urged her parents to let her go out with her friends.

Slide.Title: urgent (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: urgent (adjective) Definition: Definition: needing an immediate decision or action Synonyms: Synonyms: pressing Examples: Examples: The manager called an urgent staff meeting. Karl received an urgent message to call his wife. I need to get to this meeting now. The boss said it’s urgent! I need to get to this meeting now. The boss said it’s urgent!

Slide.Title: us (pronoun)
Slide.SlideText: us (pronoun) Definition: Definition: the form of the word “we” used after a preposition or as an object of a verb Synonyms: Synonyms: we; ourselves Examples: Examples: He said he would write to us. 2) They saw us yesterday. 3) Would you like to play with us? Would you like to play with us?

Slide.Title: use (verb)
Slide.SlideText: use (verb) Definition: Definition: to employ for a purpose; to put into action Synonyms: Synonyms: employ, utilize Examples: Examples: She used old towels to dry the dog. She doesn’t use salt in her cooking. The thief used a screwdriver to break into the car. The thief used a screwdriver to break into the car.

Slide.Title: usual (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: usual (adjective) Definition: Definition: as is normal or common; as is most often done, seen or heard Synonyms: Synonyms: common, typical Examples: Examples: I’ll meet you at the usual time. This cold weather isn’t usual for June. They’re late, as usual. They’re late, as usual.
